subject: What are the thresholds to filter bad SNPs?

messages.author: 8e733a79165c3f9e
messages.subject: What are the thresholds to filter bad SNPs?
parts:
Hello Dr. Broman (and other group members),
It is a general question regarding SNP filtering and may not be related directly to RQTL package. For a scenario of 500,000 SNPs called for linkage mapping from a data set of 100 individuals; what suitable criteria should be applied to filter bad SNPs for following points:
1) Missing Genotype: When can we consider a SNP as bad or showing excessively missing data. what's a good threshold?
2) Minor allele frequency(MAF): What MAF criteria is suitable to use?
3) What to do with SNPs with more than 2 polymorphisms: When do we consider it as a genotyping error or de novo mutation?

Thanks in advance,
Prashant

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] What are the thresholds to filter bad SNPs?
parts:
> On Apr 30, 2019, at 1:50 AM, p_waiker wrote:
>
> Hello Dr. Broman (and other group members),
> It is a general question regarding SNP filtering and may not be related directly to RQTL package. For a scenario of 500,000 SNPs called for linkage mapping from a data set of 100 individuals; what suitable criteria should be applied to filter bad SNPs for following points:
> 1) Missing Genotype: When can we consider a SNP as bad or showing excessively missing data. what's a good threshold?
> 2) Minor allele frequency(MAF): What MAF criteria is suitable to use?
I don’t think one can provide universal guidelines re missing data or MAF.
> 3) What to do with SNPs with more than 2 polymorphisms: When do we consider it as a genotyping error or de novo mutation?

I would generally just bin the less frequent alleles, but it would depend on what you’re trying to do. Software wise, it can be easier to just assume everything is biallelic, and with high density SNPs there could be little loss of information.

karl
